claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase alloy.
Untreated TC4 has intrinsically low hardness and suboptimal friction and wear properties under high-contact-stress conditions.
Plasma nitriding at approximately 700 degrees Celsius for 3–6 hours in an ammonia-based plasma can confine the nitrided region to a depth of about 10–20 micrometers.
Precisely controlled nitrogen diffusion will produce a thin, uniform near-surface layer of TiN and Ti2N precipitates.
The TiN and Ti2N precipitates will be finely dispersed within the alpha phase.
The nitriding treatment will leave the bulk alpha-plus-beta matrix intact.
Nitrogen introduced by plasma nitriding diffuses into the near-surface region and reacts with titanium to form TiN and Ti2N.
The titanium nitride phases form a hardened surface layer.
The nitride-containing surface layer increases the surface hardness of TC4.
The nitride-containing surface layer increases the wear resistance of TC4.
Use of the proposed low-temperature process prevents significant changes to the bulk microstructure.
Preventing significant bulk-microstructure changes preserves the alloy's ductility and toughness.
The treatment will increase surface hardness by approximately 60–80% relative to untreated TC4.
The treatment will significantly reduce friction relative to untreated TC4.
The treatment will significantly reduce wear rate relative to untreated TC4.
The treatment will not compromise the bulk mechanical properties of TC4.
Excessive nitrogen diffusion into the bulk could compromise the alloy's overall mechanical integrity.
The modified surface will remain effective under high-contact-stress and extreme-service conditions.
